text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has upgraded its recommendation for Brazilian state-owned power firm Cemig to long-term buy from hold following Wednesday's sale of a 33-percent voting stake in the firm to a U.S.-led consortium.

-- "For Cemig's long-suffering faithful who have watched the stock underperform the Ibovespa by 26.5 percent in the last six months, we believe now is the time to get excited about the company's prospects," Flemings analyst Walter Stoeppelwerth said.

-- A group led by U.S.-based AES Corp and Southern Co cast the sole bid to buy 32.96 percent of Cemig common stock at a Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange auction for the base price of 60.37 reais per 1,000 shares, or 1.13 billion reais. "AES will be running the show," Stoeppelwerth wrote in a report.
-- He said AES's strategy will include lifting Cemig's dividend payout to at least 85 percent and accelerate its downsizing program to reach 11,500 workers by 1998's end.
-- It also will use the firm's massive cash-flow to invest within Minas Gerais and throughout Brazil, he added.
-- Flemings has been lukewarm on Cemig over the past nine months due to its "poor operating momentum and relatively high valuation vis a vis other Brazilian utilities," he said.

-- But AES's takeover of the chief operating officer post and three seats on the board "should provide the catalyst for Cemig to deliver the margin expansion, earnings growth and dividend growth that investors have been waiting on," he added.

-- Cemig preferred was flat at 47.50 reais at 1047 local/1347 GMT in Sao Paulo and its common was untraded at Wednesday close of 46.51 reais. The LOCAL bourse was closed Thursday for Corpus Christi holiday.
